LESSON: BRAILLE EQUIPMENT (QWERTY BRAILLE KEYBOARD) • EXTEND ED KEYBOA RD

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: GRADE
Strand: Braille Writing and Reading Equipment and Materials
Topic 1.2: Braille equipment (Qwerty Braille keyboard) • Extend ed Keyboa rd
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Braille equipment (Qwerty Braille keyboard) • Extend ed Keyboa rd, part of Braille Writing and Reading Equipment and Materials in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: How is a QWERTY keyboard different from a Perkins Braille keyboard?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. explore an extended provided keyboard to identify its parts (escape key, function keys, number keys, letter keys, modifier keys, arrow keys, symbol keys) and functions (exit commands, perform specific functions with screen readers, write numbers, produce text, move cursors, execute modified codes combined to make a cord) then display for peer feedback,

2. interact with a resource person to be explained

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. explore an extended provided keyboard to identify its parts (escape key, function keys, number keys, letter keys, modifier keys, arrow keys, symbol keys) and functions (exit commands, perform specific functions with screen readers, write numbers, produce text, move cursors, execute modified codes combined to make a cord) then display for peer feedback,
2. interact with a resource person to be explained

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Braille equipment (Qwerty Braille keyboard) • Extend ed Keyboa rd together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: as learners interact with a resource person to be explained how extended keyboards are used in the

production of digital Braille work.

● Digital literacy: explore an extended provided keyboard to identify its parts (escape key, function keys, number keys, letter

keys, modifier keys, arrow keys, symbol keys) and functions (exit commands, perform specific functions with screen

readers, write numbers, produce text, move cursors, execute modified codes combined to make a cord) then display for

peer feedback.

Values:
● Responsibility: as learners explore an extended provided keyboard to identify its parts and functions then display for peer

feedback.

● cooperation: as learners work in pairs write short paragraphs on a given subject using the extended keyboard and present

for feedback,

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peer education: as learners work in pairs write short paragraphs on a given subject using the extended keyboard and present

for feedback.
